<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915520_theRebbe_327" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915520_theRebbe_327__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>These three matters correspond to wisdom, repentance, and good deeds, representing son, servant, and the will of Atzmus.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that these three matters are the three matters of wisdom, repentance, and good deeds.</t>
    <t s="2">Wisdom</t>
    <t s="3">(Torah)</t>
    <t s="4">is the matter of a son</t>
    <t s="5">(as above in section 5),</t>
    <t s="6">repentance, whose matter is that a person goes out and is nullified from his self-existence</t>
    <t s="7">(as above in section 2),</t>
    <t s="8">is analogous to the matter of accepting the yoke,</t>
    <t s="9">a servant,</t>
    <t s="10">and good deeds are the mitzvos themselves,</t>
    <t s="11">the will of Atzmus.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Through repentance, deeds become good and luminous, for the drawing of Atzmus is primarily in mitzvos, requiring the nullification of repentance.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this can be connected with the well-known explanation34</t>
    <t s="1">of the phrase "repentance and good deeds,"</t>
    <t s="2">that through repentance the deeds</t>
    <t s="3">(the deeds of the mitzvos)</t>
    <t s="4">become good deeds and luminous35,</t>
    <t s="5">for the drawing of Atzmus is</t>
    <t s="6">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="7">in the fulfillment of the mitzvos</t>
    <t s="8">(deeds),</t>
    <t s="9">and not in the nullification of repentance</t>
    <t s="10">(and acceptance of the yoke).</t>
    <t s="11">But in order that the deeds be good deeds and luminous,</t>
    <t s="12">that the drawing of Atzmus within them be revealed,</t>
    <t s="13">this is through the nullification of repentance and acceptance of the yoke.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Even in Torah study, the nullification of a servant is necessary, as one who reviews his chapter one hundred and one times differs from one who reviews it one hundred times.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, although the matter of engaging in Torah is that a person's existence</t>
    <t s="2">(his understanding and comprehension)</t>
    <t s="3">be in accordance with the Torah,</t>
    <t s="4">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="5">even in the study of Torah there must be the nullification of a servant,</t>
    <t s="6">the yoke of Torah36.</t>
    <t s="7">And this is what our sages, of blessed memory, said37</t>
    <t s="8">that one who reviews his chapter one hundred times is not comparable to one who reviews his chapter one hundred and one times,</t>
    <t s="9">because in this extra time he changes his nature and habit38,</t>
    <t s="10">for even in Torah there must be the nullification of a servant39.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
